messages:
Sam W: Heads-up: after last night's kernel-routing tweak I see a spike in KV eviction churn and a small embedding regression on INT8 longctx canaries. Anyone else?
Anya R: yup saw it. eviction.ops went up ~3x on 32k-longctx. routing now picks int8-compact much more often.
Devon L: can you paste traces/profiler output? curious slab layout changes.
Sam W: sending the key traces from the canary run: 
```
[profile] kv.slab_usage: 78% -> 94% (post-deploy)
[profile] eviction.ops/s: 18 -> 62
[kernel] route: int8-kernel-compact selected for 84% of calls (prev 12%)
[eval] avg-EMBED-L2-diff: +0.7% on canary prompts
```
Kai M: that +0.7% L2 is small but consistent with the rerank drift we observed.
Anya R: int8-compact reduces per-token resident bytes by packing slot payloads tighter and shrinking header alignment. Works great for fixed-size slots but increases fragmentation for variable-length KV pages under our slab allocator.
Devon L: fragmentation -> more small holes -> more frequent page migrations/evictions. matches the slab_usage jump.
Sam W: so routing prioritized memory footprint but didn't consider fragmentation/regrowth patterns for longctx workloads.
Kai M: we should add longctx-aware heuristics to routing and/or tweak allocator coalescing for compact-packed pages. Two levers.
Anya R: quick local experiment: force int8-legacy for longctx. results: eviction.ops/s back to ~20, memory up ~12% vs compact, embed-diff drops to +0.1%. latency unchanged.
Devon L: good signal. For routing score I suggest: score = alpha*estimated_peak_bytes + beta*expected_fragmentation_cost + gamma*reuse_score.
Sam W: what's an efficient expected_fragmentation_cost metric?
Kai M: use a recent-window normalized slab variance and hole_ratio. if hole_ratio > 0.12 or var > threshold, add penalty. cheap to compute from existing telemetry.
Anya R: allocator side: increase coalescing sweep frequency + small-slab promotion. microbench shows ~40% lower fragmentation at ~2% CPU cost. We can gate it per-deployment.
Devon L: tradeoffs: reduces eviction but costs CPU. hosted customers: probably fine; dedicated customers may prefer routing-based avoidance.
Sam W: actionable plan?
Kai M: 1) revert longctx->compact routing for canary (immediate) 2) implement routing scoring change (short-term feature flag) 3) add allocator coalescing opt-in + telemetry 4) 48h canary with eval harness monitoring embed L2, eviction.ops, p99 latency.
Anya R: I'll open a PR for routing scoring and a feature flag for allocator coalescing. I'll also emit telemetry: fragmentation_score and per-slab hole_ratio.
Devon L: I'll add a perf job to nightly: kv-frag-quant-crosswalk measuring eviction.ops and embed-l2 across BF16/FP16/INT8 with longctx distributions.
perf-bot: scheduled nightly-run: kv-frag-quant-crosswalk at 03:30 UTC. Results will post in thread.
Sam W: config snippet for ops to toggle quickly: 
```
kv_cache:
  slab_coalesce: false # enable per-deployment
  eviction_threshold: 0.75
kernel_routing:
  longctx_policy:
    prefer_compact_int8: false
    scoring:
      alpha: 0.6
      beta: 0.3
      gamma: 0.1
```
Kai M: propose canary rollout plan: 5% traffic x24h, then 25% x24h. monitor eviction.ops, p99 latency, embed-l2.
Sam W: owners: Anya (routing PR + telemetry), Devon (nightly perf job), Kai (canary rollout), Sam (ops coord). I'll post updates to #eng-runtime once PRs land.
Anya R: datasets/evals are in s3://redwood-perf/kv-longctx/microbench_v4 FYI.
Sam W: marking in-progress. will follow up with canary links and early telemetry. :thumbsup:
